title: Branch drift, drawn
subject: How far a branch has moved from main

brief.result: At a glance the reader can say whether a branch merges cleanly now, and what makes it risky.
musts: Commits ahead and behind since the merge base
How old the merge base is

ideas.title: Commit graph
ideas.encounter: Main as a line of commits; the branch leaves it at the base and runs parallel to its own tip.
ideas.helps: Where the branch started and how far each side has moved since.
ideas.sketch:

ideas.helps: The size of the gap in two numbers.
ideas.sketch:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 320 240" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="none" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">

ideas.title: Rubber band
ideas.encounter: A band from the base to main’s tip that thins as main moves on.
ideas.helps: That drift is strain which grows while the branch waits.
ideas.sketch:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 320 240" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="none" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">

ideas.title: Overlap
ideas.encounter: Two circles of changed files, one per side, with the shared files in the overlap.

ideas.title: Checklist
ideas.encounter: Four rows, each a measure with a mark where it crosses a threshold.
ideas.helps: Which measure makes the branch risky.
ideas.sketch:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 320 240" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="none" stroke="#1f2937" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">
    <text x="40" y="50" fill="#1f2937" stroke="none"  text-anchor="start">ahead</text><text x="230" y="50" fill="#1f2937" stroke="none"  font-weight="600" text-anchor="end">12</text><text x="270" y="50" fill="#1f2937" stroke="none" text-anchor="middle" >✓</text><path d="M40,66 L290,66" stroke-width="1"/><text x="40" y="96" fill="#1f2937" stroke="none"  text-anchor="start">behind</text><text x="230" y="96" fill="#1f2937" stroke="none"  font-weight="600" text-anchor="end">40</text><text x="270" y="96" fill="#1f2937" stroke="none" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="600" >!</text><path d="M40,112 L290,112" stroke-width="1"/><text x="40" y="142" fill="#1f2937" stroke="none"  text-anchor="start">overlap</text><text x="230" y="142" fill="#1f2937" stroke="none"  font-weight="600" text-anchor="end">3</text><text x="270" y="142" fill="#1f2937" stroke="none" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="600" >!</text><path d="M40,158 L290,158" stroke-width="1"/><text x="40" y="188" fill="#1f2937" stroke="none"  text-anchor="start">base age</text><text x="230" y="188" fill="#1f2937" stroke="none"  font-weight="600" text-anchor="end">9 d</text><text x="270" y="188" fill="#1f2937" stroke="none" text-anchor="middle" >✓</text><path d="M40,204 L290,204" stroke-width="1"/></svg>

grafts: the ahead and behind counts written on each line
the shared files listed under the fork
selection.rationale: The commit graph is the form readers already know from GitHub, and it places all three measures: the counts sit on its lines, the base age on its fork, and the overlap below it.
assumptions: Do readers know where a merge base is without a label?
Is three shared files enough to call a merge risky?
